title: Testing editor invocation by mocking subprocess.Popen

note.title: Testing editor invocation by mocking subprocess.Popen
answers: how to test click.edit without launching an editor
test what argv Editor passes to Popen
unit test EDITOR path parsing on Windows
note.body:
tests/test_termui.py:test_editor_path_normalization shows the pattern: `with patch("subprocess.Popen") as mock_popen: mock_popen.return_value.wait.return_value = 0; Editor(editor=cmd).edit_files(files)`.
Read argv with `mock_popen.call_args[1].get("args") or mock_popen.call_args[0][0]` and assert `call_args[1].get("shell") is None`. Patching `subprocess.Popen` works because edit_files imports subprocess locally.
Failure paths: `wait.return_value = 1` -> ClickException "Editing failed"; `side_effect=OSError(...)` -> ClickException with the OS message.
Windows-only cases go in a separate test marked `@pytest.mark.skipif(not WIN, ...)` (test_editor_windows_path_normalization). Add a parametrized case there when a new EDITOR/PAGER quoting form comes up.
note.applies: tests for click._termui_impl.Editor and pager command parsing
